subject: gov.policy
name: Cloud rules for financial service providers
milestone: Central bank guidelines issued August 2025
position_end: Central bank guidelines bar mission-critical financial-sector data from being hosted outside Tanzania and require cloud contracts to cover infrastructure redundancy and backup, encryption, multi-factor authentication, vulnerability remediation, access controls, audit rights and incident and contingency provisions
note: a sectoral residency rule; with the public-sector hosting standard it is the whole of localisation on this record

subject: gov.policy
name: Election-period internet shutdowns
milestone: A five-day nationwide blackout during the election of 2025-10-29
movement: Closed, no restoration date on file
position_end: Eight shutdowns recorded across 2025, the highest count of any African state in the monitor's data, and Tanzania listed among three African states that issued satellite shutdown orders
sources: 2026-03-01 Rising Repression Meets Global Resistance Internet Shutdowns in 2025|2026-03-05 Safeguarding Tanzania's information integrity|2026-06-09-tanzania-getting-online-digital-economy-igp-report
note: no gazetted instrument, directive or regulator order is held; the record is third-party monitoring only, and the monitor states its counts are subject to revision

subject: gov.policy
name: Electronic Data Governance Strategy
milestone: Validation workshop held 12 March 2026
position_end: A national validation workshop advanced the draft strategy, which sets interoperability, data-sharing and stewardship direction aligned with the digital economy framework, toward formal adoption; the government's own representative described it as not yet adopted
note: no draft text and no adoption date is held

subject: gov.policy
name: Government data-centre standard and hosting rule
milestone: Version 2.0 board-approved 18 February 2026
position_end: The operative standard governing public-sector data-centre siting, tiering and hosting, made under the e-government statute: it sets site-selection, power-system, cooling and utility requirements including electrical capacity, backup generators and water delivery and reservoir provision, requires public institutions to host only in government-approved environments, and bars the use of cloud platforms not owned by government
note: a localisation rule for the public sector by another name; no list of approved hosting environments is published

subject: gov.policy
name: Health-data localisation and approval conditions for AI
milestone: Stated at a university health conference 2026-07-31
position_end: Three stated requirements: health data stored inside Tanzania, healthcare AI systems approved by the relevant authorities, and local capacity to build them developed
note: a sectoral permissioning claim arriving before any national AI instrument exists; no instrument and no named approving authority, and a dedicated regulator was called for from the floor rather than announced

subject: gov.policy
name: National Broadband Strategy 2021-2026
milestone: Steering committee's first meeting, June 2026, in the strategy's final year
position_end: The ministry confirmed the 2021-2026 strategy actively overseen at its steering committee's first meeting, with the regulator reporting 94 per cent high-speed internet coverage and 35 per cent 5G access; a parliamentary committee separately confirmed the 758-tower project complete with 304 towers upgraded to 4G and 5G
note: no primary text of the strategy is locatable, and its steering committee met for the first time in its final year

subject: gov.policy
name: National Data Management Framework
milestone: A stakeholder process reported under way, completion targeted January 2026
position_start: Stakeholder drafting under way, targeted for January 2026
position_end: Unchanged; the base holds no record of completion, publication or slippage past the target
note: positioned within a continental data policy framework; eleven months with nothing later on file

subject: gov.policy
name: National ICT Policy 2016 and its successor plan
milestone: Stakeholder consultation on a successor infrastructure plan, March 2026
position_start: The 2016 policy, revising the 2003 one, is the standing instrument; a 2023 draft successor went out for stakeholder review and no evidence of its enactment was located
position_end: A ministry consultation in March 2026 opened a new national information and communication technology infrastructure development and construction plan with an accompanying construction guideline, and the 2026/27 budget of 222.589 billion shillings set eight priorities including backbone strengthening, technology parks and rural connectivity
note: a ten-year-old policy with a draft successor unenacted for three years is the standing frame

subject: gov.policy
name: National Technology Roadmap
milestone: Draft completed and presented at a stakeholder discussion, August 2026
position_end: Drafted by the education, science and technology ministry, forecasting the country’s technology needs over the next 25 years across 13 sectors; not adopted, and no publication or approval date is on file

subject: gov.policy
name: Tanzania Digital Trust Initiative
milestone: Launched at an inaugural forum, 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-08
position_end: Launched as a multi-stakeholder body to coordinate cybersecurity, data privacy, artificial-intelligence governance and payment security across government, industry and academia, founded by a security firm with a privacy professionals' association and a fintech association, and naming the data protection commission, the ICT commission and the private sector federation among its partners; the same forum published a digital trust outlook report and inaugurated an East Africa to Gulf Cooperation Council corridor for cross-border regulatory dialogue, secure payments and artificial-intelligence governance
note: a private-sector-founded body naming public regulators as partners; no constitution, funding, membership list or statement of the regulators' role in it is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to Information Act 2016
milestone: A nationwide internet shutdown taken to the regional court, December 2025
position_start: The founding right-to-information statute, gazetted 30 September 2016 and in force from 1 July 2017, applying to mainland Tanzania only
position_end: The statute is unamended, but the regulator suspended the country's leading civic discussion and whistleblowing platform for 90 days under the online content regulations in September 2025, and a rights organisation filed a reference at the East African Court of Justice in December 2025 challenging the nationwide internet shutdown of 29 October to 4 November 2025 as an unlawful restriction on access to information
note: no request or appeal statistics under the statute are published for any year

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrimes Act and the critical infrastructure regime
milestone: Critical infrastructure registration opened 19 June 2026
position_start: The principal cybercrime statute, in force since September 2015 and consolidated in 2023, criminalising illegal access, interception, data interference and computer-related fraud and forgery, and providing for the protection of critical information infrastructure
position_end: The ministry opened a six-month registration window from 19 June to 19 December 2026 activating the critical-infrastructure regime across finance, health, water, energy, mining, transport, agriculture, industry, education and defence, with mandatory 24-hour incident reporting and penalties of at least 100 million shillings, three times the loss caused, or five years' imprisonment
note: eleven years between the statute's critical-infrastructure sections and the notice that activates them

subject: gov.legislate
name: e-Government Act and its technical standards
milestone: Data-centre and application standards board-approved 18 February 2026
position_start: The 2019 statute mandates integration and interoperability of government systems, establishes the authority's data-sharing and exchange platform mandate, and provides the basis for its technical data standards
position_end: Two board-approved standards were issued under it in February 2026: a data-centre standard setting site, power, cooling and utility requirements that approved government hosting environments must meet, and an application standard requiring secure development-lifecycle controls, vulnerability testing, audit logs and privacy by design, with open interoperable design and government-controlled source-code hosting
note: the companion public data centre rules gazetted in 2026 could not be captured verbatim and are not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Finance Act 2026 amendment to the Electronic Transactions Act
milestone: Section 13 of the Electronic Transactions Act (Cap. 442) amended, 2026-06-30
position_start: No ministerial power to prescribe which payments must be made electronically
position_end: The Minister for Finance may prescribe by Gazette order which payments must be made electronically — the power the mandatory electronic payments order of the same date was made under — and proof of electronic payment is required before a transfer of land, a building or a motor vehicle can be approved
note: the land, building and motor-vehicle requirement is a substantive obligation in its own right and is not part of the scheduled transaction classes the order lists

subject: gov.legislate
name: Financial consumer protection amendment regulations
position_end: Unchanged; providers must protect consumer financial and personal information in accordance with the data-protection Act
sources: 2025-06-27 Key Highlights of the Bank of Tanzania Financial Consumer Protection Amendment Regulations GN 298 of 2025
note: the dormant-account period moved from five to twelve months, with complaint maxima of twelve hours for mobile money and fourteen days for credit, and fines of TZS 1m a day; the data-protection cross-reference is what wires the payments regime into the data regime

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Payment Systems Act and its consumer rules
milestone: Complaint-handling guidelines replaced in November 2025
position_start: The founding payment-systems statute of 2015 regulates payment-system licensing, electronic payment instruments and electronic money and assigns licensing and supervision to the central bank
position_end: New complaint-handling guidelines replaced the 2015 set, mandating standardised, no-fee, multi-channel complaint handling with digital channels required of providers operating digital platforms, statutory resolution timelines and a central-bank appeal; separate regulations gazetted in December 2025 bring non-interest banking windows into a prudential framework requiring a compliant core banking system
note: no complaint volume or resolution-time series is published against the guidelines

subject: gov.legislate
name: Online content and cybercrime regulation
note: no Tanzanian instrument on online content, VPN registration or cybercrime is held: the only trace is a bibliographic citation inside an unrelated report

subject: gov.legislate
name: Registration and Identification of Persons Act
milestone: Implementation reported to a parliamentary committee, 19 August 2026
position_start: The founding 1986 statute establishing registration of persons and identity-card issuance, still in force as the 2023 consolidated edition
position_end: Unchanged in law; the home affairs minister presented the identity authority's and immigration department's implementation report to parliament's foreign affairs, defence and security committee in August 2026
note: the statute predates the digital identity built on it by three decades; no amendment covering the digital layer is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Review of more than 1,000 laws for technology investment
milestone: Announced 2026-08-12
position_end: The government says it will review more than 1,000 laws, including the public-private partnership act, the companies act and financial legislation, to build a regulatory framework supporting artificial intelligence, digital commerce and technology investment under the 2050 development vision
note: no list of statutes, sequencing, responsible body or timetable is stated, and no consultation route is named

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act
milestone: Revised Edition 2019 of Act No. 9 of 2015
position_start: Establishes the statistics bureau as a continuing body, its governing board and the national statistical system, and is the principal statute for the production, coordination and dissemination of official statistics
position_end: Unchanged; a 2023 revised edition of the same statute is also held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Tax identifier display for online traders
milestone: Made by the Minister for Finance at Dodoma, 30 June 2026, as Government Notice No. 158G
position_end: Businesses trading on social media platforms must display their tax registration number or tax compliance certificate on their profile pages, under a new sub-regulation 58(2) of the Tax Administration (General) Regulations, 2016, made under the Tax Administration Act
note: the instrument itself is now held and settles three things the secondary accounts left open: it was made by the Minister for Finance rather than the revenue authority, it amends regulation 58 of the 2016 regulations, and the display duty is the whole of the new sub-regulation, with no penalty provision and no non-resident provision attached to it

subject: gov.protect
name: Certified Data Protection Officer programme
milestone: Launched 2026-07-14 by the commission with the open university
position_end: The university trains and assesses and the commission certifies, targeting government, finance, telecommunications, healthcare, education and technology
sources: 2026-07-14 OUT, PDPC Launch National Data Protection Programme
note: the capacity answer to the statutory mandatory-officer duty; no intake number, fee or first cohort date is on file

subject: gov.protect
name: National Advisory Committee on Online Child Protection and Safety
milestone: Committee established; 1,811,212 children reached with online-safety education
position_end: A national advisory committee on online child protection and safety has been established, bringing in the ministry responsible for information and communication technology to give technical advice and support strategy development on the risks children face online, including those posed by artificial intelligence. The community development ministry told parliament on 31 August 2026 that an education campaign aimed at children, parents, guardians and the wider community had reached 1,811,212 children across all 26 mainland regions
note: a precise reach figure with no methodology behind it, and a committee with no published membership, terms of reference, meeting record or output; the answer was given to a parliamentary question rather than in a report

subject: gov.protect
name: Personal Data Protection Act, 2022
milestone: Commenced 2023-05-01, with regulations in force
position_start: In force, with a supervisory commission, a registration duty, a mandatory officer requirement and a breach-notification duty; Part V sets the transborder data-flow regime, requiring an adequacy assessment and commission-authorised safeguards for transfers to states without adequate protection
position_end: Unchanged text; no amendment and no new regulations recorded in the window
sources: 2023-06-13-personal-data-protection-act-2022|2026-02-09 Notification obligations arising from personal data breaches in Tanzania
note: the primary text is now held, including Part V and the section establishing the commission

subject: gov.protect
name: Registration and data-protection-officer compliance regime
milestone: On-site inspections to begin 2026-08-31
position_start: The registration deadline had expired on 2025-04-30 and commission activity was confined to risk training and awareness; the minister gave a final three-month registration ultimatum in January 2026 and directed the commission to prepare nationwide compliance audits
position_end: On-site compliance inspections of institutions collecting and processing personal data begin on 31 August 2026, after preliminary desk assessment found limited understanding of legal obligations, inaccurate registration information, difficulty implementing data-subject rights, and personal data transferred abroad outside the statutory procedure. Inspections verify registration status, the performance of data-protection officers, and how data is collected, processed, stored and transferred, with remedies from rectification directives upward
note: the base holds no count of registered controllers and no inspection outcome, fine or enforcement decision after the April 2026 start date

subject: gov.protect
name: Tax-credential display rule for social-media businesses
milestone: Rule in effect, reported 2026-08-12
position_end: Businesses selling on social media must display tax credentials — a taxpayer identification number, tax clearance certificate or certificate of registration — on their public pages; digital creators and online traders have objected that publishing the credentials exposes them to impersonation and fraud, and no data-protection assessment or redress route is published
note: the objections are those of named creators and traders reported by the paper, not a regulator finding; the instrument behind them is now held, and it carries no penalty provision and says nothing about how a published credential is to be protected from the impersonation the objectors describe

subject: gov.regional
name: EAC regional AI strategy
milestone: National stakeholder consultations held in Tanzania 2026-02-12
position_end: Drafting under way, with ministers agreeing at a regional conference to pursue harmonised rules and retention of AI value in East Africa
sources: 2026-03-31 EAC moves to create unified AI Sovereignty bloc
note: no adoption date, text or Tanzanian ratification step is on file, and the source is held as an excerpt

subject: gov.regional
name: Knowledge exchange with Somalia on government digital systems
milestone: Delegation received 2026-08-28
position_end: a Somali government delegation studying the labour and employment digital systems in Dodoma on 28 August 2026, and Somalia seeking to learn from the public-service digitalisation experience more broadly

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional data-governance commitment under the digital integration project
milestone: Third steering committee, Nairobi, 5 to 6 May 2026
position_end: All eight partner states of the East African Community, Tanzania among them, reaffirmed at the project's third steering committee their commitment to inclusive regional data-governance frameworks supporting secure cross-border data flows
note: a reaffirmation of commitment rather than a harmonised instrument; the project's own supervision report a month later records that none of the governance instruments it was to produce exists

subject: gov.standards
name: Adoption of international standards
milestone: Sustainability and climate-risk guidelines issued for 2025
position_start: The accountancy board's 2018 pronouncement assigns full international financial reporting standards, public-sector accounting standards and the small-entity variants by entity category, effective for periods from April 2019; international financial reporting and auditing standards were adopted from July 2004
position_end: The standards bureau's October 2025 compulsory list carries more than 130 mandatory standards enforceable under the standards statute, including identical or closely referenced international electrotechnical adoptions, and the central bank's supervision report for 2025 confirms new sustainability and climate-related financial-risk guidelines aligned to the international sustainability standards, alongside continued Basel implementation
note: none of the adopted standards on this record is digital or information-security specific

subject: gov.standards
name: Interoperability framework and government application standards
milestone: Application standards version 3.0 board-approved February 2026
position_start: The 2016 interoperability framework defines nine technical-standards areas — interconnection, access, collaboration, data integration and the rest — that public institutions must follow, and is still the referenced framework in the 2026 capability maturity model
position_end: A board-approved application standard of February 2026 requires secure development-lifecycle controls, vulnerability testing, audit logs and privacy by design for government applications including artificial-intelligence-enabled ones, and mandates open interoperable design with government-controlled source-code hosting; a service directory launched in June 2026 with more than 500 institutions onboarded under a directive to connect to the government service bus
note: the framework is ten years old and still the reference; no conformance regime or compliance count is published against either instrument

subject: gov.standards
name: Regulatory cooperation on satellite communications with Kenya
milestone: Two-day benchmarking visit to the Kenyan regulator, August 2026
position_end: The communications regulator undertook a two-day benchmarking visit to its Kenyan counterpart to exchange experience and practice in regulating satellite communications. No memorandum, harmonised rule, licensing change or follow-up is published
note: a visit reported in a trade account, carried here because the base holds no other statement of how this regulator approaches satellite licensing; it will settle or lapse on whether anything is issued after it

subject: gov.discourse
name: Licensed online media
milestone: Quarterly count to June 2026
position_start: Six online content aggregators, 74 weblogs, 221 online television stations, 51 cable television operators and 10 online radio stations at March 2026
position_end: Five online content aggregators, 66 weblogs, 210 online television stations and 49 cable television operators at June 2026, with online radio the exception at 12; the regulator said the quarterly decline was not evidence of a shrinking digital economy, pointing to July 2026 changes to the online content regulations that cut licence fees by 90%, from TZS 1m to TZS 100,000 for aggregators and from TZS 500,000 to TZS 50,000 for ordinary online content providers

subject: gov.discourse
name: Litigation over platform account suspensions
milestone: Complaint filed in San Mateo County Superior Court, 21 August 2026
position_end: An activist and social-media influencer suing a platform company in the United States, alleging that her accounts were disabled at the direction of the government; the complaint was filed on 21 August 2026 in San Mateo County Superior Court
note: The complaint itself is now held, so the filing date and forum are read from the court record rather than from a report of it.

subject: gov.discourse
name: Online gendered violence against election candidates
position_end: Documented as cyclical across successive elections in a two-country civil-society study, with no state measurement held against it
note: a civil-society research organisation's study of online gendered violence against candidates across election cycles in Tanzania and Côte d'Ivoire; the base holds no regulator, electoral-commission or platform figure for the same phenomenon, so this is the only measurement of it on file and it is the researcher's own

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic state appropriation for digital transformation
milestone: Estimates for Vote 68 presented to Parliament 2026-04-30
movement: No change, domestic development finance unchanged
position_end: Vote 68 proposed at TZS 222,589,451,000 for 2026/27 against TZS 291,533,139,000 approved for 2025/26, split TZS 13.15bn recurrent and TZS 209.44bn development; domestic development finance is unchanged to the shilling at TZS 98.48bn while external development finance falls from TZS 178.57bn to TZS 110.96bn, taking the external share of development spending from 64% to 53%; TZS 147,768,795,247 of the 2025/26 vote had been released by March 2026, 50.6%
note: the vote falls 24% year on year and the whole reduction is external finance

subject: finance.mou
name: Bilateral digital-cooperation tracks with Brazil, Poland and Russia
milestone: Cooperation frameworks agreed at an international summit; memoranda proposed, none signed
position_end: Frameworks agreed with two states on AI strategy, digital government and cybersecurity research, and youth and technology-skills agreements in drafting with a third
note: no signed instrument, amount or timetable is held for any of the three; three tracks opened in one week

subject: finance.mou
name: Digital economy memorandum with Huawei
milestone: Signed in Shanghai by the ministry's permanent secretary, witnessed by the minister
position_end: Cooperation named across ICT infrastructure, AI, digital public service infrastructure, developing local professionals, and manufacture and assembly of digital equipment
note: no commitment amount, term or financing structure is stated in the ministry's own release, and device manufacture is placed inside a vendor memorandum rather than an industrial policy

subject: finance.mou
name: Zanzibar broadband memorandum with a second operator
milestone: A memorandum signed covering broadband, digital inclusion and public services
position_start: A memorandum signed with no value
position_end: A memorandum signed with no value; no follow-through on file at 2026-08-06
note: it reads against the priced twenty-year agreement the same agency signed ten months later

subject: finance.new
name: Concessional loan for an AI and digital technology training institute
milestone: US$170m approved at the lender's 159th management committee, 23 August 2026
position_end: A Korean development cooperation fund committed US$170m to build an AI and digital technology training institute, approved at its 159th management committee and announced on 23 August 2026; it is the fund's first AI project, and the planned institute is to offer four programmes
note: an approval rather than a signature or a disbursement, and the fund's first artificial-intelligence project anywhere; no site, intake, curriculum, start date or disbursement schedule is published

subject: finance.new
name: Digital Tanzania Project
milestone: Board approval of a US$150m operation covering broadband, digital government, digital financial services and digital skills
position_end: US$150m committed, active
note: the largest single commitment in the base, scheduled to close in 2026, and nothing in the base marks its closure; no disbursement figure and no completion report

subject: finance.new
name: Payment-rails credit facility
milestone: A US$25m credit facility announced, extendable to US$50m
position_end: US$25m secured and extendable to US$50m, for international remittance and stablecoin corridors
note: debt rather than equity; the base's prior record for the same company is a different instrument, and no local-currency figure is published

subject: infra.connect
name: 5G deployment
milestone: The regulator's quarterly report to 2026-03-31
position_end: 1,804 facilities on 10,084 towers, 32.83% population coverage and 11.04% geographic, with every region holding at least three base stations
note: facilities up 139% from 754 in June 2024, with data consumption up from 426 to 932 petabytes

subject: infra.connect
name: 636-mast programme
milestone: Due March 2027
position_end: 636 masts due March 2027, with a second programme of 280 masts stated under way
note: no cost, financier or completion date for the second programme is stated

subject: infra.connect
name: 758-tower rural connectivity project
milestone: Restated to an international policy forum, 4 September 2026
position_end: A TZS 126bn project - TZS 55bn from the World Bank and TZS 71bn from the universal service fund - has connected 8.5 million people across more than 1,400 villages through 758 completed 4G towers, the communications minister told an international telecommunication policy forum on 4 September 2026, alongside 800 digital clubs established through the regulator, Wi-Fi at 100 public locations and computer laboratories in 250 public schools, all under the national development vision to 2050 and the national digital economy strategy for 2024 to 2034
note: the same 758 towers and 8.5 million people are now stated to two audiences four months apart with no change in the figures, and the three priorities the country proposed at the forum - affordable access, digital skills and artificial intelligence, secure and inclusive infrastructure that protects personal data - carry no instrument or target with them

subject: infra.connect
name: Active mobile subscriptions and penetration
milestone: Regulator's own quarterly sector report for the quarter to June 2026
position_end: 117m telecom subscriptions and 89.7% internet penetration for the quarter ending June 2026 on the regulator's own count, with internet subscriptions up 6.48% to 62.79 million, data consumption up 11.65% to 1,041 petabytes, mobile-money subscriptions up 7.5% to 87.05 million, and smartphone penetration at 44.74% against featurephone penetration of 83.38%
note: the regulator's own quarterly report is now held first-hand, published on its statistics library dated 2026-08-10; the figures this row carries came to it through a newspaper's selection from that report

subject: infra.connect
name: Backbone users connected in Dodoma Region
milestone: The figure given to the minister 2026-07-24
position_end: 65 people connected in the whole region
note: the government's own figure; no national connected-user total is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet exchange points
milestone: Six exchanges operating on the association's own account
position_end: The service providers' association operates six exchanges — the Dar es Salaam exchange plus nodes at Arusha, Dodoma, Mbeya, Mwanza and Zanzibar; a carrier-neutral data-centre operator joined the peering community in September 2025, and a second developer passed 380 million dollars of committed capital in July 2026 with a Tanzanian carrier-neutral facility offering exchange and peering connectivity in its pipeline
note: the association's page carries no dateline; no member count, traffic figure or local-traffic share is published for any of the six

subject: infra.connect
name: Kenya border terrestrial fibre link
milestone: Launched 2026-07-29
position_start: The backbone connected to Mombasa on the same route, with no launched cross-border service
position_end: Launched by both ministers, with the national backbone integrated with submarine cable capacity
note: no capacity, cost or financing is stated, and its relation to the 2025 connection is not reconciled in the base

subject: infra.connect
name: Kigoma-Kalemie fibre across Lake Tanganyika
milestone: Both governments reaffirmed the project, 2026-09-05
position_end: A national fibre-optic cable from Kigoma to Kalemie in the Democratic Republic of Congo through Lake Tanganyika, which the foreign minister said the two countries would fast-track alongside a standard gauge railway link through Burundi and the establishment of a joint economic commission
note: stated at a farewell meeting for the Congolese ambassador; no route survey, cost, financing, landing point or delivery date is published

subject: infra.connect
name: Kilimanjaro One submarine cable
milestone: Announced 2025-11-12
position_end: 1,900 km from Dar es Salaam to Mauritius with two branches; construction stated from 2026 and completion late 2027
note: no construction start, contractor or cost has been confirmed in the base since the announcement

subject: infra.connect
name: Leading operator network investment and coverage
milestone: Annual general meeting for the year ended 2026-03-31, reported 2026-08-21
position_end: 27.7 million customers and capital expenditure up 85.1% to TZS 323.9 billion for the year ended 2026-03-31, with 444 new 4G and 25 new 5G sites lifting 4G population coverage to 76.3%, mobile money customers up 22.6%, 466 rural sites built since 2013 under the government rural connectivity programme and a TZS 53.5 billion dividend approved
note: the operator's own figures, reported at its annual general meeting; not a regulator series

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile tariffs and device affordability
milestone: Bundle data at 9.35 shillings a megabyte, quarter ending March 2026
position_start: Industry-average bundle data tariffs fell 2.0 per cent from 2.12 to 2.08 shillings a megabyte while bundle voice tariffs rose, on-net by 14.2 per cent and off-net by 4.7 per cent, in the quarter to September 2025
position_end: Basic voice at 29 shillings a minute and bundle data at 9.35 shillings a megabyte for the quarter to March 2026, with mobile broadband penetration at 42.5 per cent and smartphone penetration at 32.83 per cent; an operator and vendor device-financing offer put a 5G router at 80,000 shillings upfront and 80,000 a month for twelve months with unlimited internet up to 10 Mbps
note: the two tariff series are quoted on different bases, 2.08 and 9.35 shillings a megabyte, and the regulator publishes no reconciliation between them

subject: infra.connect
name: National ICT Backbone investment commitment
position_end: a prime ministerial commitment to continue increasing investment in the communications sector, including strengthening the national backbone and raising funding for the rural communications fund

subject: infra.connect
name: National ICT Broadband Backbone
milestone: Zanzibar expansion reviewed by the President of Zanzibar, 2026-08-24
position_start: 13,820 km laid of a 16,280 km planned total at April 2025, 109 of 139 districts, all 111 service delivery points done; TZS 73bn for 2025/26
position_end: 15,167 km at December 2025 at 2,000 Gbps, all mainland regional headquarters and 122 of 139 districts, linked to seven neighbouring countries; in one region 942.5 km built against 65 citizens connected region-wide (2026-07)
note: contradiction resolved 2026-08-09: the two figures were 13 months apart, not in conflict. 16,280 km is the planned total and 13,820 km the length laid at April 2025 (FY2025/26 budget speech); 15,167 km is the length at December 2025 (minister's WTISD 2026 statement). The 'over 15,000 km' quoted at WSIS in July 2026 is that December 2025 figure, correctly stated. Built as a state network: the regional manager states phase one connected government offices and public institutions, with individual citizens only next

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite broadband service
milestone: Live in Tanzania as of November 2025
position_start: A distribution deal covering Tanzania among fourteen markets announced 2025-05-06, service not live
position_end: Live, with direct-to-cell and backhaul reseller arrangements alongside
sources: 2026-01-01 Starlink Partners with Airtel & Vodacom From Rival to Ally|2025-05-06-airtel-spacex-starlink-afrika
note: a month-precision date; no subscriber, licence or pricing figure for Tanzania is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Second operator fibre-to-the-home and business service
milestone: Fibre-to-the-home launched in Dodoma, 2026-08-26
position_end: Home, business and institutional fibre launched in the capital across Ilazo, Ipagala, Swaswa, Mjini Kati and Barabara za Namba, with coverage to extend progressively across the city as demand grows. No subscriber, premises-passed, speed or price figure is stated; the operator has launched fibre-to-the-home in Dodoma with plans to widen coverage across the city, on a stated 300 billion shilling investment

subject: infra.connect
name: Smartphone users and penetration
milestone: The regulator's quarterly report to 2026-03-31
position_end: 28.5m users and 42.5% penetration
note: the user count fell quarter on quarter while the percentage rose, and the base does not reconcile the two; the regulator names low smartphone penetration and a 23.7% geographic broadband gap as sector challenges

subject: infra.connect
name: Tower and fibre public-private handover
milestone: Handed to government 2026-04-11
position_start: Under construction since the May 2023 launch: 758 new towers plus 304 upgrades, not yet transferred
position_end: 758 towers and about 1,100 km of fibre transferred to government across three corridors plus metro fibre
note: the prior date is month-precision

subject: infra.connect
name: TTCL fibre-to-the-home programme

subject: dpi.registry
name: National addressing and postcode system
milestone: An address count given with a continental postal certification
position_start: 85% of Tanzanians reached since the 2022 census, a population rate
position_end: More than 12.9m residential addresses registered, 29 systems interconnected and international certification obtained
sources: 2026-02-09 Tanzania registers 12 million housing addresses to boost digital governance|2024-07-10 Tanzania ramps up national physical address registration
note: the wiki holds that the population rate and the address count are not derivable from one another and must not be charted together

subject: dpi.registry
name: Permanent National Voters' Register
milestone: 37,647,235 registered voters for the 2025 general election
position_start: Established by the 2024 elections act, which repealed the 1985 and 1979 election laws and provides for both a preliminary and a permanent national register
position_end: 37.66 million voters on the register ahead of the 2025 general election, revised to 37,647,235 once Zanzibar's finalised figures were reconciled; the electoral commission explained the growth as about 3,113,931 previously eligible but unregistered people now registered, after an opposition party disputed the numbers

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register and the integrated revenue administration system
milestone: Integrated system went live 9 February 2026
position_start: The tax administration statute requires taxpayer registration and identifier issuance linked to the national identification number
position_end: The revenue authority completed its integrated domestic revenue administration system with pre-launch verification of migrated taxpayer records ahead of a 9 February 2026 go-live, and the 2026/27 budget commits it to integrating that system with the property register for direct data exchange and to registering buildings, owners' identity and tax details and all local traders
note: no registered-taxpayer count and no migration-error rate is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Under-five birth registration coverage
milestone: 68% in 2025 stated by the constitutional and legal affairs minister, reported 2026-08-20
position_end: 68 per cent registered in 2025 against 55 per cent in 2020 on the minister's own series, with a stated target of 100 per cent by 2030; the base separately holds 65 per cent reported a week earlier, about 60 per cent for 2022 and a range of 61 to 76 per cent over five years on different bases
note: the base holds several differently-based estimates for this measure and does not reconcile them to one series - and the two newest are a week apart from the same minister, 65% reported 2026-08-13 and 68% for 2025 reported 2026-08-20, which is the clearest available demonstration that the figure is quoted rather than published

subject: dpi.registry

milestone: Briefing on what establishment would require, August 2026
position_end: A blueprint and a follow-on briefing set out what a unified, dynamic social registry would require to map and identify poor households in support of poverty reduction

subject: dpi.registry

milestone: Operational since June 2025, with more than 450,000 digital addresses assigned
position_start: Operational since June 2025 with more than 450,000 addresses assigned

note: twelve months with no update is itself the finding; the first payoff was student finance

subject: dpi.mis
name: Agriculture and fertiliser information systems
milestone: Both systems described at an agricultural exhibition
position_end: One system holds farmer records, manages ministry institutions and issues agricultural permits; the other monitors manufacturers, importers and distributors against indicative prices
note: no user counts, spend or timeline are given for either

subject: dpi.mis
name: Cradle-to-career learner tracking
milestone: Announced November 2025
position_end: The permanent secretary announced plans for a system following students from early childhood through higher education, prompted by the gap between 907,803 students selected for Form One in 2022 and 595,816 sitting Form Four in 2025
note: an announcement; no design, budget or timetable is stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Criminal Justice Single Window System
milestone: Announced in the 2026/27 budget statement
position_end: The minister for constitutional and legal affairs announced a draft national criminal justice policy and a single-window system integrating information-technology platforms across police, courts and prosecution

subject: dpi.mis
name: Customs system and the trade single window

position_end: A Zanzibar single window launched in June 2026 replaced visits to more than 14 institutions for trade clearance, and a government-backed baseline assessment found 33 of 92 inter-agency trade services digitised and still fragmented across nine agencies
note: the revenue authority's own launch page for the enhanced customs system is unreachable, so the standing position rests on the audit

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digital legal assistant for access to justice
milestone: Disbursement recorded for the 2025 activity year
position_end: A bilateral aid programme funded a digital legal assistant enabling access to justice for women
note: a commitment record rather than a service report; no user count, case volume or outcome is stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education sector management information system

position_end: The permanent secretary directed institutions to fast-track integration of their own digital platforms so enrolment and other statistics are reachable without manual requests — a move from building the central system to connecting the institutional ones
note: no go-live date, connected-institution count or data-quality statement is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Government asset management information system
milestone: Enforcement tightened, 2026-08-09
position_end: In use as the central electronic system for recording and monitoring public assets, with the finance ministry tightening enforcement and citing major investments including a hydropower project at about TSh6tn and a railway at about TSh10.6tn; legal backing comes through amendments to the Public Finance Act and the Public Assets Management Regulations 2024

subject: dpi.mis
name: Health management information system
milestone: Procurement agenda set out 2026-09-01
position_start: A fragmented ecosystem of eighteen systems, with the platform in all district councils since 2013 carrying over 90% of flows

subject: dpi.govtech

position_end: In service alongside AI-enabled echocardiography, contactless vital-signs monitoring and robotic surgery; no patient volumes, spend or procurement route stated

subject: tech.ai

The ministry's permanent secretary said in March 2026 that the national strategy was completed, and Tanzania's own July 2026 statement to the United Nations global dialogue describes an implemented national artificial intelligence strategy framework of 2026 while acknowledging the legislative gap and that liability and oversight rules were still being developed; independent assessments published at the end of July still record no adopted national instrument, with work proceeding off existing digital, data-protection and science frameworks. subject: tech.ai

position_end: A board-approved government application standard of February 2026 adds secure development-lifecycle controls, vulnerability testing, audit logs and privacy by design for government applications including artificial-intelligence-enabled ones

Founders and the fund told a Dar es Salaam session that partnerships with banks and mobile operators remain the main barrier to scale, citing banks assessing early-stage firms through a static lens, the commoditisation of the core processing layer as institutions build technology in house, limited patient capital, technical talent shortages, regulatory and tax uncertainty and the cost of acquiring customers

note: growth is agent build-out rather than branch build-out, and the council says so itself

subject: include.access
name: Financial inclusion index
milestone: The council's annual report records the 2025 reading
position_start: 0.81 (2024), with access at 0.84 and usage at 0.78
position_end: 0.83 (2025), with access at 0.87 and usage at 0.79
note: the series ran 0.69, 0.81, 0.83 and is flattening; access moved three points and usage one, which the regulator's own report reads as people reaching the system and not using it

subject: include.access
name: Provision for refugees and displaced people
milestone: 2022-2027 disaster management strategy
position_end: The 2022-2027 national disaster management strategy expressly lists refugees and internally displaced people among vulnerable groups and commits to mainstreaming their needs across disaster-risk management
note: there is no standalone statute on internally displaced people, and the citizen unique identifier regime carries no provision for non-citizens on this record

subject: include.access
name: Statutory machinery for participation in local decisions
milestone: Consolidated 2023 edition of the founding statute
position_end: The founding statute establishes village assemblies, village councils and ward development committees, which is the statutory machinery through which citizens take part in local decisions
note: nothing digital attaches to it on the record, and no participation rate or meeting record is published

subject: include.access
name: Third National Financial Inclusion Framework
milestone: Mid-term evaluation covering December 2023 to December 2025
position_end: The 2023-2028 framework is in implementation with the inclusion index as its headline metric. Its mid-term evaluation, covering December 2023 to December 2025 and produced by the central bank and the national council for financial inclusion, is the framework's own scorecard on whether it has moved beyond access toward active usage, service quality and financial health. On the published reading of it the access dimension has essentially been won, and the framework's distinctive claim - the shift to usage, quality and household financial health - is what the remaining half of its term has to deliver
note: the evaluation reaches this base through an analytical commentary rather than as a document; no usage, quality or financial-health figure from it is held, so the framework's own scorecard cannot be read here

subject: include.access
name: Universal service fund rural site programme
milestone: 133 fund sites completed, marked at a Dodoma event
position_end: 133 sites completed, with about 45% of the operator's Tanzanian sites rural
sources: 2026-04-13 Helios Towers completes 133 UCSAF sites to expand rural connectivity in Tanzania
note: no levy rate, fund balance, appropriation or programme-wide site target is held anywhere in the base: the fund is named but never quantified

position_end: EUR 3,000,000 committed, active

milestone: First national assessment, October 2025
position_end: The two statistics bureaux published a first national assessment of the skills, infrastructure, policy and data-sharing constraints on big-data use, positioned as extending the master plan beyond censuses, surveys and administrative sources

milestone: 257,405 establishments in the 2024 update
position_end: 257,405 establishments, a rise of 17.3 per cent in a year, built by integrating mainland and Zanzibar tax records with other administrative sources — a finding and a sampling-frame improvement at once

subject: data.statistics
name: Statistics Act and the national statistical system
milestone: Revised Edition 2023 of the founding statute
position_end: The founding statute continues the statistics bureau as an autonomous public office, establishes the national statistical system, and places the initiation of official censuses and surveys under the Statistician General
note: two revised editions of the same statute are held, 2019 and 2023

subject: data.statistics
name: Tanzania Statistical Master Plan phase two
milestone: 88.9 per cent implemented at the July 2026 steering review
position_start: A 2022/23 to 2026/27 national strategy for the development of statistics, published in December 2021 and budgeted at 384 million dollars for harmonisation, production and infrastructure across the statistical system
position_end: The finance ministry's steering committee reported 88.9 per cent implementation since 2022/23 and approved the 2026/27 work plan and budget, ahead of the plan's completion in June 2027
note: the implementation figure is the committee's own; no output-level accounting behind it is held

subject: data.open
name: External fiscal transparency assessment
milestone: Assessed as not meeting the minimum requirements, 2026
position_start: Assessed in the previous review as not meeting the minimum requirements
position_end: Assessed again as not meeting the minimum fiscal transparency requirements, over a review period running to 31 December 2025
note: an external assessment on a foreign government's own criteria; it is the only recurring transparency measure the base holds for this country

subject: data.open
name: Open-data instruments and the statistical portal
status: Implemented, no general open-data policy adopted
milestone: Integrated statistical portal in service
position_end: No general national open data policy has ever been adopted — one drafted in 2016 and 2017 was submitted and its lack of official adoption recorded — so what governs release is sectoral: the statistics bureau's 2024 dissemination policy sets an open-access tier and principles of transparency, accessibility, timeliness and confidentiality; the procurement authority's 2025 policy mandates publication of procurement data in open contracting format through its portal; and the two statistics offices run an integrated portal bringing administrative, demographic and survey data together
note: the portal's own page carries no dateline and its date is this run's retrieval date; a third-party account puts the launch at 11 May 2026 and is not first-hand

position_end: A budget line, with no design, launch date, operator or cost broken out

subject: geopol.usa

position_end: A March 2023 package includes an export-financing memorandum of up to 500 million dollars covering digital technology and a 5G-security and cyber-cooperation memorandum; since then a Tanzanian organisation was selected for a hyperscaler social entrepreneur accelerator with cloud and artificial-intelligence support, and a data-centre developer whose major shareholder is American-founded passed 380 million dollars of committed capital with a Tanzanian carrier-neutral facility in its pipeline

milestone: Joint statement of 3 November 2022
position_end: A joint statement establishing the comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership, covering investment, infrastructure, trade, energy, minerals and digital and green development alongside implementation of the belt and road memorandum
note: the digital content is one clause of a general partnership statement; no digital-specific Chinese instrument with Tanzania is held

subject: geopol.eu

position_end: The first partnership dialogue under the Samoa Agreement produced a joint communique recording European commitments of EUR 726 million for 2021 to 2027, a planned security dialogue and Tanzania's first request under the European Peace Facility; no standalone digital instrument is named in it
